A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MergeBO research. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including Appendix A in v3 and Appendices A–B in v4.

before.justification: Section 4, Table 2, and Figure 1 report the authors' experiments comparing MergeBO and BOPS-H on permutation optimization benchmarks.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B.3 report original experiments, including expanded baseline comparisons in Tables 2–3 and Figure 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the Merge feature kernel in Equation 4, and the hybrid TTP kernel in Equation 5 are retained. Stabilized comparisons were already described in v3; v4's expanded explanation and diagram do not establish a changed proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate 15-dimensional TSP and QAP, 30-dimensional floor planning and cell placement, and the same three 280-city TTP instances with 279 or 837 items. Added comparators reuse this coverage; Rodinia remains unevaluated.

E2.justification: V3 evaluates only BOPS-H against MergeBO. V4 adds TuRBO across the benchmarks and randomly subsampled comparison features on the low-dimensional benchmarks in Table 2. Appendix B.3 and Table 3 additionally evaluate Spearman's footrule across all seven reported problems.

E3.justification: V4 introduces comparator-specific protocols: TuRBO searches a continuous unit hypercube with argsort projection, and the randomized control matches Merge's feature dimensionality. The original benchmarks retain their stated acquisition procedures, iteration budgets, and regret metrics; no revision of those existing settings is disclosed.

E4.justification: V4 adds a dimension-matched randomized-feature ablation to test structured information versus compression alone. Appendix B.3 further examines the trade-off using an O(n), right-invariant footrule representation. These provide new empirical mechanism analyses beyond v3's Merge–Mallows comparison; a rough low-dimensional timing comparison is also added.

E5.justification: Both retain 20 low-dimensional trials, 50 TTP trials, trial-index seeds, mean and standard-deviation reporting, and the binomial sign test at p < 0.05. Additional comparator results extend these practices without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V4 adds results for three comparators and revises existing TTP values. For example, Merge's TTP1 final regret changes from 22.5×10^3 to 23.0×10^3 and AUC from 21.5×10^5 to 20.5×10^5, while its 50/50 wins remain. It also reports approximately 10% slower low-dimensional kernel computation. The updated TTP2 plot conflicts with Table 2.

T1.justification: The kernel definitions, positive-definiteness argument, and Stirling-based encoding lower bound are retained. Appendix B.2 relocates the existing lower-bound discussion. Equation 6 supplies the standard formula for the previously mentioned footrule distance; no new proof or substantive revision of the theoretical argument is provided.

C1.justification: The sorting-based framework, compact lossless representation, and dimension-dependent advantage remain the core claims. V4 broadens the introduction's and conclusion's high-dimensional performance claim to include TuRBO and general BO comparisons, rather than BOPS-H alone.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations linking randomized-feature underperformance to structural information and the TuRBO gap to specialized permutation modeling. It also discusses restoring right-invariance through additional comparisons, excludes the randomized baseline from TTP because of projection difficulties, and explains footrule behavior through local additivity and exploitation. The timing discussion newly qualifies low-dimensional computational efficiency.

D1.justification: V4 supplies a project source-code link, identifies the CAS computational-resource provider, and describes Python recursion, list slicing, and deepcopy overhead. V3 supplied the BOPS baseline link and core library/settings information but lacked these disclosures. The PDFs establish the new access statement, not independently verified repository contents.

R1.justification: V4 removes background citations to Alatartsev et al., Blau et al., Sun and Giles, and Wen et al. Previously cited TuRBO and Spearman's footrule become substantive evaluated alternatives. The central positioning against Mallows remains; the corrected Knuth reference denotes the same work.

P1.justification: V4 condenses the introduction into comparison-category bullets and reorganizes the method explanation. Existing sorting-choice and lower-bound discussions move into Appendices B.1–B.2, with some expansion. Author information, citation formatting, and acknowledgements also change, while the main section sequence and much of the prose remain.

P2.justification: V4 adds a feature-construction diagram, expands and redraws the convergence figure with comparator curves and revised axes, and substantially restructures Table 2 around additional methods and win counts. New Table 3 redisplays existing results alongside Spearman results. Algorithm 1 and existing tables also move.

improvement.justification: The added baselines, controlled ablation, and code-access information address weaknesses in v3's single-baseline evaluation. However, v4 introduces a material reporting conflict: Figure 2(f) ends near 2.3×10^4 for Merge on TTP2, whereas Table 2 reports 14.9×10^4; v3's corresponding plot and table agreed near 14.5×10^4. This undermines confidence in central high-dimensional evidence, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain.
